blocks.text: Relevance measures whether a response actually addresses what was asked, a distinct evaluation dimension from faithfulness, whether claims are grounded in given context, and accuracy, whether information is factually correct, a response can score well on both of those and still fail to genuinely answer the actual question.

This topic covers relevance as its own distinct dimension, query relevance versus context relevance in a RAG system, measuring it with an LLM judge, and why a faithful, accurate response can still be irrelevant to what was genuinely being asked.
1. What Relevance Means as an Evaluation Dimension

blocks.alt: What Relevance Means as an Evaluation Dimension
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972759-249814688.png
Relevance evaluates whether a response actually engages with and addresses the specific question or request, rather than providing information that is technically true but genuinely beside the point.
2. Relevance vs Faithfulness vs Accuracy
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972759-444800137.png

These three dimensions answer genuinely different questions, faithfulness asks whether claims trace back to provided context, accuracy asks whether information is factually or classification correct, relevance asks something else entirely, does this response actually address what was asked in the first place.

blocks.text: 3. Query Relevance
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972908-670733797.png

Query relevance checks the direct match between what a user actually asked and what the response actually addresses, a technically correct, well written response about a related but genuinely different topic than what was asked scores poorly on this dimension even if every individual sentence in it is true.
4. Context Relevance in a RAG System

blocks.alt: Context Relevance in a RAG System
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972909-120730253.png

This connects directly to retrieval prompting, covered in the earlier RAG Prompting module, in a RAG system, relevance also applies one level earlier, to the retrieved content itself, was the content retrieval actually surfaced genuinely relevant to the query, independent of whether the final generated answer used it well.
5. Measuring Relevance With an LLM Judge

blocks.alt: Measuring Relevance With an LLM Judge
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972909-811534939.png

This connects directly to LLM-as-judge, covered in the previous topic, relevance is well suited to this approach, giving a judge model the original query and the response, and asking it to score specifically how directly the response addresses that exact query.

code.content:
judge_prompt = (
    f"Query: {query}\nResponse: {response}\n"
    "On a scale of 1-5, how directly does this response address the query? "
    "Score only relevance, not factual correctness."
)

blocks.text: 6. A Faithful, Accurate Response Can Still Be Irrelevant

blocks.alt: A Faithful, Accurate Response Can Still Be Irrelevant
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972910-124118305.png

This is the core insight this topic adds, a response can be perfectly grounded in provided context and perfectly factually correct while still not actually answering what was asked, a user asking about a product return policy who receives an accurate, well grounded answer about the product warranty policy instead has been given a response that fails specifically on relevance, despite passing every other check.

blocks.title: This is why evaluation needs all three dimensions together
blocks.content: A system that only checks faithfulness and accuracy could pass every check while consistently answering a slightly different question than what users actually asked, relevance is the dimension that specifically catches this failure mode.

blocks.text: 7. A Worked Relevance Evaluation Example

A user asks "how do I cancel my subscription" and receives an accurate, well grounded response explaining subscription pricing tiers instead, faithfulness and accuracy checks might both pass, since the pricing information is genuinely correct and grounded, but a relevance check immediately flags this as a poor response since it never actually addresses cancellation.
8. Relevance Drift Across a Conversation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473972910-722151924.png

This connects directly to the multi-step reasoning coherence concerns covered in the earlier Agent Prompting module, relevance can also be tracked across a multi-turn conversation, checking whether later turns remain relevant to the original request, or whether the conversation has gradually drifted toward a different topic without anyone noticing.
9. Combining Relevance With Other Metrics

A genuinely thorough evaluation practice tracks relevance alongside faithfulness and accuracy, all three together, rather than any single one alone, give a much more complete picture of response quality, catching different, complementary failure modes each dimension is specifically designed to reveal.
Worked Example

A team evaluating their support assistant tracks only faithfulness and accuracy, both scoring consistently well, user satisfaction remains surprisingly low despite these strong scores, adding a relevance check reveals the assistant frequently answers a closely related but genuinely different question than what was actually asked, a pattern the faithfulness and accuracy metrics alone had no way to catch.

Addressing this specific relevance gap, by improving how the assistant interprets the actual intent behind a query before responding, meaningfully improves user satisfaction in a way the previously tracked metrics alone could never have revealed.
Common Mistakes

items: Assuming a faithful, factually accurate response is automatically also a relevant one
Tracking only faithfulness and accuracy, missing the specific failure mode relevance is designed to catch
Not checking relevance at the retrieval stage separately from the final generated response in a RAG system
Ignoring relevance drift across a multi-turn conversation, where later turns gradually wander from the original topic

blocks.text: Practice

Take a query and a response that is factually accurate but subtly addresses a related, different question, score it for faithfulness and accuracy separately from relevance, and confirm how a response can pass the first two checks while clearly failing the third.
Key Takeaway

Relevance evaluates whether a response actually addresses what was asked, a distinct dimension from faithfulness and accuracy that catches a genuinely different failure mode, a technically correct, well grounded response that answers the wrong question, and a complete evaluation practice needs to track all three dimensions together rather than relying on any single one alone.
